input.sha256_scope: The committed classic-v1-benchmark-page/input.png, which one of the three cases uses. The other two are deterministic synthetic pages generated by formula on both sides.
input.provenance: No new input pixels. One case reuses an already-committed fixture PNG; the other two are generated by a closed-form expression reproduced identically in the capture tool and the Rust test.

upstream.capture_method: Re-captured by tools/capture_layout_oracle.py, which imports and executes the pinned PaddleX operators. The v1 capture transcribed them and was wrong twice: it fed BGR where ReadImage(format='RGB') converts, and it divided by 255 where Normalize multiplies by a folded 1/255. Both were found by the table cell oracle, which shares this code path and was captured by execution from the start.

limitations: One of three cases -- synthetic-1, 297x421 -> 800x800 -- inherits the cubic resize's open divergence and is bounded rather than matched exactly; the other two are exact.
Detections come from a real inference run against the pinned artifact. They are recorded so the decode can be tested, not as an accuracy claim.
Supersedes schema v1, whose tensors were wrong in two ways; see upstream.capture_method.
